metadata.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Linear Convolutional Networks
metadata.authors: Suriya Gunasekar, Jason D. Lee, Daniel Soudry, Nathan Srebro

nodes.name: Linear fully connected network
nodes.statement: An $L$-layer feed-forward network with dense layers $\u_l\in\bR^{D_{l-1}\times D_l}$ computing $\h_l=\u_l^\top\h_{l-1}$, with composite predictor $\P_{full}(\u)=\u_1\u_2\ldots\u_L\in\bR^D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multi-layer linear network with dense connections; the effective predictor is the product of weight matrices.

nodes.name: Linear convolutional network
nodes.statement: An $L$-layer linear network whose hidden layers apply circular convolution $\h_l[d]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{D}}\sum_{k=0}^{D-1}\u_l[k]\,\h_{l-1}[(d+k)\bmod D]$ with full-width filters $\u_l\in\bR^D$, followed by a fully-connected output layer with weights $\u_L\in\bR^D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multi-layer network with full-width 1D circular convolutional layers and a fully connected output.

nodes.name: Linear diagonal network
nodes.statement: Network with diagonal interlayer maps: $\P_{diag}(\u)=\diag(\u_1)\diag(\u_2)\ldots\diag(\u_{L-1})\u_L$ for $\u_l\in\bR^D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear network where each interlayer transformation is restricted to a diagonal matrix.

nodes.name: Discrete Fourier basis representation
nodes.statement: For $\z\in\bR^D$, $\hat{\z}[d]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{D}}\sum_{p=0}^{D-1}\z[p]\,\omega_D^{pd}$ where $\omega_D=\e^{-\frac{2\pi\ci}{D}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discrete Fourier transform of a real vector using primitive $D$-th roots of unity.

nodes.name: Convergence in direction
nodes.statement: A sequence $\w[t]$ converges in direction to limit direction $\bar\w^\infty$ if $\bar\w^\infty=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\w[t]}{\norm{\w[t]}}$ exists.
nodes.statement_clean: Sequence of vectors converges in direction when its normalized version has a limit.

nodes.name: Bridge ($\ell_p$) penalty
nodes.statement: $\norm{\z}_p=\big(\sum_{i=1}^{D}|\z[i]|^p\big)^{1/p}$; a norm for $p\ge 1$ and a quasi-norm for $p<1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quasi-norm version of $\ell_p$ for $0<p<1$, called the bridge penalty.

nodes.name: Homogeneous polynomial parameterization
nodes.statement: A multivariate polynomial map $\P:\bR^P\to\bR^D$ is homogeneous of degree $\nu$ if $\P(\alpha\mathbf{v})=\alpha^\nu\P(\mathbf{v})$ for all $\alpha\in\bR$ and $\mathbf{v}\in\bR^P$.
nodes.statement_clean: A polynomial map that scales with a fixed power of its argument.

nodes.name: Implied predictor-space penalty $\c{R}_{\P}(\w)$
nodes.statement: $\c{R}_{\P}(\w)=\inf_{\u:\P(\u)=\w}\norm{\u}_2^2$, the minimum parameter $\ell_2^2$ norm achieving predictor $\w$ under parameterization $\P$.
nodes.statement_clean: The minimum squared parameter norm needed to realize a given linear predictor.

nodes.name: Clarke sub-differential
nodes.statement: $\partial^\circ f(\w)=\mathrm{conv}\{\mathbf{v}:\exists(\z_k)_k,\,\z_k\to\w\text{ and }\nabla f(\z_k)\to\mathbf{v}\}$, the local sub-differential operator.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalized gradient (Clarke sub-differential) for non-smooth, non-convex functions.

nodes.name: Empirical risk minimization for linearly parameterized networks
nodes.statement: $\min_{\u\in\c{W}}\;\c{L}_{\P}(\u):=\sum_{n=1}^N \ell(\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\u)},y_n)$ for a parameterization $\P:\c{W}\to\bR^D$ and per-example loss $\ell$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the sum of per-example losses on a linearly separable dataset, parameterized through a network mapping.

nodes.name: Hard-margin SVM (max-margin $\ell_2$ separator)
nodes.statement: $\w^*_{\ell_2}=\argmin_{\w\in\bR^D}\norm{\w}_2^2\;\st\;\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\w}{\x_n}\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the unit-margin separator with smallest $\ell_2$ norm.

nodes.name: Bridge-penalty maximum margin in Fourier domain
nodes.statement: $\min_{\w}\norm{\hat{\w}}_{2/L}\;\st\;\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\w}{\x_n}\ge 1$, where $\hat{\w}$ is the DFT of $\w$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the bridge $\ell_{2/L}$ penalty of the Fourier transform of $\w$ subject to unit margin.

nodes.name: Parameter-space $\ell_2$ margin problem
nodes.statement: $\min_{\u\in\bR^P}\norm{\u}_2^2\;\st\;\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\u)}\ge 1.$
nodes.statement_clean: Minimum-$\ell_2$ parameter $\u$ subject to unit margin in the induced predictor.

nodes.name: Predictor-space induced penalty margin problem
nodes.statement: $\w^*_{\c{R}_{\P}}=\argmin_{\w}\c{R}_{\P}(\w)\;\st\;\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\w}{\x_n}\ge 1$, with $\c{R}_{\P}(\w)=\inf_{\u:\P(\u)=\w}\norm{\u}_2^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimum induced-penalty linear predictor subject to unit margin.

nodes.name: Gradient descent on parameterized network loss
nodes.statement: Iteratively update parameters $\u[t+1]=\u[t]-\eta_t\nabla_{\u}\c{L}_{\P}(\u[t])$ to minimize $\c{L}_{\P}$ over the network parameterization $\P$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard gradient descent on the parameter loss; the implicit bias of this iteration is the paper's central object.
input: Loss $\ell$ with tight exponential tail (e.g. $\ell(\hat y,y)=\exp(-\hat y y)$)
output: Induced linear-predictor sequence $\w[t]=\P(\u[t])$ converging in direction to $\bar\w^\infty$

nodes.name: Standing assumptions on gradient descent iterates
nodes.statement: (i) $\u[t]$ minimize the objective $\c{L}_{\P}(\u[t])\to 0$; (ii) $\u[t]$ and consequently $\w[t]=\P(\u[t])$ converge in direction to a separator with positive margin $\min_n y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\bar\w^\infty}>0$; (iii) the loss gradients $\nabla_{\w}\c{L}(\w[t])$ converge in direction.
nodes.statement_clean: GD iterates drive the loss to zero, converge in direction with positive margin, and produce loss gradients that converge in direction.

nodes.name: Coordinate-wise phase convergence (convolutional case)
nodes.statement: For all $d$, $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\w}^{(t)}[d]}}\to\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}}$, where the limit phase is also assumed to exist for coordinates with $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=0$.
nodes.statement_clean: The phase of every Fourier coordinate of the iterates converges, including at zero-magnitude coordinates.

nodes.name: Implicit bias for linear fully connected networks
nodes.statement: Under the standing assumptions, gradient descent on $L$-layer fully connected linear networks converges in direction to the hard-margin SVM solution: $\bar\w^\infty=\w^*_{\ell_2}/\norm{\w^*_{\ell_2}}$ where $\w^*_{\ell_2}=\argmin_{\w}\norm{\w}_2^2\,\st\,\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\w}\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: GD on fully connected linear networks of any depth has the same hard-margin SVM bias as direct GD on $\w$.
assumptions: Standing assumptions (AssumP449.1): $\c{L}_{\P_{full}}(\u[t])\to 0$; $\u[t]$ converges in direction to a positive-margin separator; $\nabla_{\w}\c{L}(\w[t])$ converges in direction
conclusions: The limit is independent of the depth $L$

nodes.name: Implicit bias for depth-2 linear convolutional networks
nodes.statement: Under the standing assumptions plus phase convergence, gradient descent on a $2$-layer linear convolutional network converges in direction to $\bar\w^\infty=\w^*_{\c{F},1}/\norm{\w^*_{\c{F},1}}$ where $\w^*_{\c{F},1}=\argmin_{\w}\norm{\hat{\w}}_1\,\st\,\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\w}{\x_n}\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two-layer convolutional networks induce a max-margin solution with minimum $\ell_1$ norm of the Fourier transform.
assumptions: Step sizes $\eta_t$ smaller than the local Lipschitz constant at $\u[t]$
$\c{L}_{\P_{conv}}(\u[t])\to 0$ and $\u[t]$ converges in direction with positive margin
Phase of Fourier coefficients $\hat{\w}^{(t)}$ converges coordinate-wise (AssumP449.2)

nodes.name: Implicit bias for linear convolutional networks of any depth $L$
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-net}, the limit direction $\bar\w^\infty=\lim_{t\to\infty}\P_{conv}(\u[t])/\norm{\P_{conv}(\u[t])}$ is a positive scaling of a first-order stationary point of $\min_{\w}\norm{\hat{\w}}_{2/L}\,\st\,\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\w}{\x_n}\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Depth-$L$ convolutional networks bias gradient descent toward stationary points of the bridge $\ell_{2/L}$ penalty applied to the Fourier transform.
assumptions: All conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-net} (TP449.2) at any depth $L$
conclusions: For $L>2$, $p=2/L<1$ so the objective is non-convex (a quasi-norm bridge penalty)

nodes.name: Implicit bias for homogeneous polynomial parameterization
nodes.statement: For any homogeneous polynomial $\P:\bR^P\to\bR^D$, under the standing assumptions on gradient descent iterates $\u[t]$ for $\c{L}_{\P}(\u)$ with exponential loss, the limit direction $\bar\u^\infty=\lim_{t\to\infty}\u[t]/\norm{\u[t]}_2$ is a positive scaling of a first-order stationary point of $\min_{\u}\norm{\u}_2^2\,\st\,\forall n,\,y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\u)}\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: GD on any homogeneous polynomial parameterization biases toward $\ell_2$ stationary points in parameter space.
assumptions: $\P$ a homogeneous polynomial of finite degree $\nu$
$\u[t]$ and $\w[t]=\P(\u[t])$ converge in direction with positive margin
conclusions: Equivalently, KKT conditions of the parameter-space $\ell_2$ margin problem hold at a positive scaling of $\bar\u^\infty$

nodes.name: Hard-margin SVM bias of GD on linear logistic regression (cited)
nodes.statement: For any linearly separable dataset and initialization, gradient descent on logistic loss with the direct parameterization $\w$ converges in direction to $\w^*_{\ell_2}/\norm{\w^*_{\ell_2}}$, the hard-margin SVM solution.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited result that GD on linear logistic regression converges in direction to the SVM solution.
nodes.origin_citation: Soudry et al. 2017 (Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent)

nodes.name: Fourier representation of convolutional parameterization
nodes.statement: For full-dimensional convolutions, $\w=\P_{conv}(\u)$ satisfies $\hat{\w}=\diag(\hat{\u}_1)\ldots\diag(\hat{\u}_{L-1})\hat{\u}_L$, where $\hat{\u}_l\in\b{C}^D$ are the Fourier coefficients of $\u_l\in\bR^D$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convolutional networks act as diagonal networks on Fourier coefficients.
assumptions: $\u=[\u_l\in\bR^D]_{l=1}^L$ are full-width convolutional filters and final dense layer

nodes.name: Equivalence of GD updates between convolutional and Fourier-diagonal networks
nodes.statement: For all $l$, $\c{F}\Delta\u[t]_l=\hat{\u}_l^{(t+1)}-\hat{\u}_l^{(t)}=-\eta_t\nabla_{\hat{\u}_l}\hat{\c{L}}_{\P_{diag}}(\hat{\u}^{(t)})$, so GD on $\c{L}_{\P_{conv}}$ in the spatial domain equals GD on $\hat{\c{L}}_{\P_{diag}}$ in the Fourier domain (up to DFT).
nodes.statement_clean: GD on convolutional parameters is equivalent under DFT to GD on a complex diagonal network.

nodes.name: Form of $\c{R}_{\P_{full}}$ for fully connected networks
nodes.statement:
For fully connected networks of any depth $L>0$, $\c{R}_{\P_{full}}(\w)=\min_{\u:\P_{full}(\u)=\w}
orm{\u}_2^2=L
orm{\w}_2^{2/L}=\mathrm{monotone}(
orm{\w}_2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Implied predictor-space penalty for FCNs is a monotone function of the $\ell_2$ norm.
assumptions: Fully connected linear network with $L>0$ layers and parameters $\u=[\u_l\in\bR^{D_{l-1}\times D_l}]_{l=1}^L$

nodes.name: Form of $\c{R}_{\P_{diag}}$ for diagonal networks
nodes.statement: For depth-$L$ diagonal networks with parameters $\u=[\u_l\in\bR^D]_{l=1}^L$, $\c{R}_{\P_{diag}}(\w)=L\norm{\w}_{2/L}^{2/L}=\mathrm{monotone}(\norm{\w}_{2/L})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Implied penalty for diagonal networks is a monotone function of the bridge $\ell_{2/L}$ quasi-norm.
assumptions: Depth-$L$ linear diagonal network with parameters $\u=[\u_l\in\bR^D]_{l=1}^L$

nodes.name: Form of $\c{R}_{\P_{conv}}$ for convolutional networks
nodes.statement: For depth-$L$ convolutional networks, $\c{R}_{\P_{conv}}(\w)=L\norm{\hat{\w}}_{2/L}^{2/L}=\mathrm{monotone}(\norm{\hat{\w}}_{2/L})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Implied penalty for convolutional networks is a monotone function of the bridge $\ell_{2/L}$ quasi-norm of the Fourier transform.
assumptions: Depth-$L$ linear convolutional network with parameters $\u=[\u_l\in\bR^D]_{l=1}^L$

nodes.name: Gradients of exponential-loss converge to span of support vectors (cited)
nodes.statement_clean: Limit direction of the loss gradients lies in the positive span of the support vectors of $\bar{\w}^\infty$.
nodes.origin_citation: Lemma 8 of Gunasekar et al. 2018 (Characterizing Implicit Bias)

nodes.name: Auxiliary lemma on $\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}$ in convolutional GD analysis
nodes.statement: For $\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}$ in eq. \eqref{eq:cn-ud+}, for all $d$ such that $\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]\neq 0$, $\b{u}_d^{(t)}\to\infty$ and $\boldsymbol{\tau}_d^{(t)}/\b{u}_d^{(t)}\to 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Auxiliary technical lemma controlling perturbation terms in the depth-2 convolutional analysis.

nodes.name: Stolz-Cesaro theorem (cited background)
nodes.statement: If $\{a_k\},\{b_k\}$ are real sequences with $\{b_k\}$ strictly monotone and divergent, and $\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{a_{k+1}-a_k}{b_{k+1}-b_k}=L$ exists, then $\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{a_k}{b_k}=L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discrete L'Hopital-style lemma used to control telescoping ratios.
nodes.origin_citation: Theorem 1.22 of Muresan 2009 (Concrete Approach to Classical Analysis)

nodes.name: Sub-differential of $\norm{\hat{\w}}_1$
nodes.statement: $\partial^\circ\norm{\hat{\w}}_1=\{\hat\z:\forall d,\,|\hat\z[d]|\le 1\text{ and }\hat{\w}[d]\ne 0\Rightarrow \hat\z[d]=\e^{\ci\boldsymbol{\phi}_{\hat{\w}}[d]}\}$.

nodes.name: Sub-differential of $\norm{\hat{\w}}_p$ for $p<1$
nodes.statement: $\forall p<1,\;\partial^\circ\norm{\hat{\w}}_p=\{\hat\z:\hat{\w}[d]\ne 0\Rightarrow \hat\z[d]=p\,\e^{\ci\boldsymbol{\phi}_{\hat{\w}}[d]}|\hat{\w}[d]|^{p-1}\}$.

nodes.name: Convolutional-network output formula
nodes.statement: $f_{\u}(\x)=\big(((\x\star\u_1)\star\u_2)\ldots\star\u_{L-1}\big)^\top\u_L$, the $L$-layer convolutional composite map.

nodes.name: Circular convolutions and zero-padding
nodes.statement: The paper uses circular convolutions with $1/\sqrt{D}$ scaling for cleaner analysis. Similar behavior is expected for zero-padded convolutions, but is not analyzed here.

nodes.name: Restriction to exponential / tight-exponential-tail losses
nodes.statement: The analysis is for exponential loss $\ell(u,y)=\exp(-uy)$; the results should extend to strictly monotone losses with a tight exponential tail (e.g. logistic), following the techniques of Soudry et al.

nodes.name: Non-convexity of the bridge-penalty problem for $L>2$
nodes.statement: For $L>2$, $p=2/L<1$ and the bridge-penalty maximum-margin problem is non-convex and intractable in the worst case; the result thus only guarantees convergence to a first-order stationary (sub-stationary) point.

nodes.name: Stationary points in parameter vs. predictor space are not equivalent
nodes.statement: Although global minimizers of the parameter-space and predictor-space margin problems coincide, their stationary points generally do not; a stationary point of \eqref{eq:l2bias} may be just feasible (not stationary) for \eqref{eq:Rwmargin}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:metathm} (homogeneous polynomial parameterization)
nodes.statement: Show that a positive scaling of $\bar{\u}^\infty$ satisfies the KKT conditions of the parameter-space $\ell_2$ margin problem, by combining homogeneity, Lemma~\ref{lem:grad-conv}, and a Stolz-Cesaro argument on the cumulative GD update.

nodes.name: Set up scaling representation of iterates
nodes.statement:
Write $\u[t]= ar{\u}^\infty g(t)+ delta[t]_{\u}g(t)$ with $g(t)=
orm{\u[t]}$ and $ delta[t]_{\u}	o 0$; deduce $\w[t]/
orm{\w[t]}	o\P( ar{\u}^\infty)/
orm{\P( ar{\u}^\infty)}=: ar{\w}^\infty$ via homogeneity of $\P$.

nodes.name: Express loss-gradient and Jacobian via scaling
State KKT conditions for parameter-space $\ell_2$ margin problem
nodes.statement: Identify primal feasibility ($y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\u)}\ge 1$), dual feasibility ($\alpha_n\ge 0$, $\alpha_n=0$ off support), and stationarity $\u=\nabla_{\u}\P(\u)\sum_n\alpha_n y_n\x_n$ for first-order stationary points.

nodes.name: Establish primal feasibility via homogeneous scaling
nodes.statement: Choose $\gamma=(\min_n y_n\innerprod{\x_n}{\P(\bar\u^\infty)})^{-1/\nu}$ so that $\tilde{\u}^\infty=\gamma\bar\u^\infty$ has unit margin.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:grad-conv} for support-vector decomposition
nodes.statement: Use the cited lemma to write $\bar{\z}^\infty=\sum_{n\in S_\infty}\alpha_n y_n\x_n$ with $\alpha_n\ge 0$, giving the dual certificate.

nodes.name: Sum GD updates and isolate dominant term
Apply Stolz-Cesaro to control error term
Conclude stationarity in parameter space
nodes.statement: Divide by $\norm{\u[t]}$ and take the limit to obtain $\bar\u^\infty\propto\nabla_{\u}\P(\bar\u^\infty)\bar{\z}^\infty$, completing the KKT verification.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:fcn} (FCN)
nodes.statement: Specialize Theorem~\ref{thm:metathm} to $\P_{full}$, then express $\nabla_{\u_1}\P_{full}(\u)\z=\z\u_{2:L}^\top$ to deduce $\bar{\u}_{1:L}^\infty\propto\bar{\z}^\infty$, the SVM dual certificate.

nodes.name: Apply meta-theorem and identify $\bar\u_{1:L}^\infty=\P_{full}(\bar{\u}^\infty)$
nodes.statement: Note $\P_{full}$ is homogeneous of degree $L$; set $\tilde{\w}^\infty=\gamma\bar\u_{1:L}^\infty$ with unit margin and dual certificate $\bar{\z}^\infty=\sum_{n\in S_\infty}\alpha_n y_n\x_n$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:grad-conv}.

nodes.name: Specialize parameter-space stationarity to $\u_1$
nodes.statement: From eq. \eqref{eq:p-stat-fcn} and $\nabla_{\u_1}\P(\u)\z=\z\u_{2:L}^\top$, get $\bar\u_1^\infty=\bar\gamma\,\bar{\z}^\infty\bar\u_{2:L}^{\infty\top}$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\bar\u_{1:L}^\infty\propto\bar{\z}^\infty$
nodes.statement: Multiply by $\bar\u_{2:L}^\infty$ to get $\bar\u_{1:L}^\infty=\bar\gamma\,\bar{\z}^\infty\norm{\bar\u_{2:L}^\infty}^2\propto\bar{\z}^\infty$, verifying the SVM KKT conditions.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorems~\ref{thm:conv-net}-\ref{thm:conv-net-l} (convolutional networks)
nodes.statement: Reduce convolutional GD to complex diagonal GD via Lemmas~\ref{lem:fft-conv} and \ref{lem:fft-gd}, derive sub-stationarity from parameter-space stationarity, and for $L=2$ prove the dual bound $\bar\gamma|\hat{\bar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\le 1$ by analyzing the dynamics of $\b{u}_d^{(t)}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to Fourier-diagonal network
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:fft-conv} to express $\hat{\w}^{(t)}=\odot_l\hat{\u}^{(t)}_l$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:fft-gd} to identify GD updates of the Fourier coefficients with GD on a complex diagonal network.

nodes.name: Specialize parameter-space stationarity to convolutional case
nodes.statement:
From eq. \eqref{eq:c-p-stat} and the formula $
abla_{\u_l}\P_{conv}(\u)\z=\c{F}^*(\prod_{l'
e l}\diag(\hat{\u}_{l'}^*))\c{F}\z$, derive $\hat{ ar\u}_l^\infty= ar\gamma(\odot_{l'
e l}\hat{ ar\u}_{l'}^{\infty*})\odot\hat{ ar\z}^\infty$.

nodes.name: Extract magnitude and phase relations
nodes.statement: From $|\hat{\bar\u}_l^\infty[d]|^2=\bar\gamma|\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]||\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]|\,\e^{\ci(\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty}-\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty})}$, deduce phase equality $\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}}=\e^{\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]}}$ and magnitude relation $|\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]|^{2/L}=\bar\gamma|\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]||\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]|$.

nodes.name: Case split on depth $L$
nodes.statement: For $L>2$ ($p<1$), the magnitude/phase relations are exactly the sub-stationarity condition for $\norm{\hat\w}_p$. For $L=2$ ($p=1$), additionally need the dual bound $\bar\gamma|\hat{\bar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\le 1$ at coordinates with $\hat{\bar\w}^\infty[d]=0$.

nodes.name: Define $\b{u}_d^{(t)}$ and study its dynamics ($L=2$)
nodes.statement: Set $\b{u}_d^{(t)}=\hat{\u}_1^{(t)}[d]\e^{-\ci\phi_{\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]}}+\hat{\u}_2^{(t)*}[d]$; using Lemma~\ref{lem:cn-lemma} obtain $\b{u}_d^{(t+1)}=[1+\eta_t p(t)(|\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]|+\bdelta_d^{(t)})]\b{u}_d^{(t)}$.

nodes.name: Compare ratios $\kappa_{d,d'}^{(t)}$ and conclude dual bound
nodes.statement: Show that $|\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]|>|\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d']|$ implies $\kappa_{d,d'}^{(t)}=|\b{u}_d^{(t)}/\b{u}_{d'}^{(t)}|\to\infty$; together with the limiting magnitude, this forces $\hat{\bar{\w}}^\infty[d]=0$ whenever $|\hat{\bar\z}^\infty[d]|<1/\bar\gamma$, so $\bar\gamma|\hat{\bar{\z}}^\infty[d]|\le 1$ for all $d$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:fft-conv}
nodes.statement: Use $\c{F}\c{F}^*=I$, the identity $\c{F}(\h\star\u)=\hat{\h}\odot\hat{\u}^*$, and iterate over layers to conclude $\hat{\w}=\hat{\u}_1\odot\hat{\u}_2\odot\ldots\odot\hat{\u}_L$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:fft-gd}
nodes.statement: Differentiate $\ell(\innerprod{\x}{\P_{conv}(\u)},y_n)$ in spatial domain, use the Fourier representation from Lemma~\ref{lem:fft-conv}, and apply $\c{F}^*\c{F}=I$ to identify $\c{F}\nabla_{\u_l}\c{L}_{\P_{conv}}=\nabla_{\hat\u_l}\hat{\c{L}}_{\P_{diag}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{prop:fcn} ($\c{R}_{\P_{full}}$)
nodes.statement:
Lower bound: by AM-GM applied to layer norms, $
orm{\w}_2^{2/L}\le rac{1}{L}\sum_l
orm{\u_l^*(\w)}_2^2$. Upper bound: explicit construction $ ar\u$ with rank-1 layers achieves $
orm{ ar\u}_2^2=L
orm{\w}_2^{2/L}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma for $\c{R}_{\P_{diag}}$
nodes.statement: By coordinate-wise AM-GM, $\sum_d|\w[d]|^{2/L}\le\frac{1}{L}\sum_d\sum_l|\u_l^*(\w)[d]|^2=\frac{1}{L}\c{R}_{\P_{diag}}(\w)$. The reverse bound is achieved by the explicit factorization $\bar\u_l[d]=|\w[d]|^{1/L}$ (with sign on layer 1).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma for $\c{R}_{\P_{conv}}$
nodes.statement: Use orthonormality of the DFT ($\norm{\u}_2^2=\norm{\hat\u}_2^2$) to reduce to the diagonal-network argument applied to $\hat{\u}$, $\hat{\w}$.
